notes: Account: mid-market product company building a contextual in-app assistant and doc search across user docs/KB.
Primary asks: low-latency chat (p99 <= 250ms), predictable cost per active user, EU data residency for subset of data.
Initial preference: try Hosted API for fast time-to-value; if POC unit economics favorable, move to Dedicated for guaranteed throughput.
Cost sensitivity: finance wants ARR model <= $120k for year-one inference spend; target per-conversation token cost goal provided.
POC traffic profile: 200 concurrent users, avg 350 tokens/generation, peak ~320 rps during batch window (client sim script attached).
Security: require SSO/SAML, audit logs retention 12 months, KMS integration for key rotation, and EU residency for EU tenant data.
- Batching: showed 2.0-3.0x cost reduction vs naive single-request serving for their mix (better at 16-32 token sequences).
- KV/Prefix caching: for multi-turn flows we recommended session-level KV cache with 60s TTL; expected 15-25% token savings for typical sessions.
- Quantization profiles: recommended fp16->int8/4 quant candidate for non-retrieval-heavy calls; SE to run quality regression suite against golden prompts.
- Unit economics: built simple spreadsheet (drive link) showing Hosted cost at scale vs Dedicated reserved capacity; tipping point at ~12M tokens/day where Dedicated is >30% cheaper.
Quote from engineering lead: "If we can hit p99 < 250ms and keep cost per active MAU below threshold we'll proceed to reserved pool."

POC plan (agreed): 2-week Hosted POC instrumented with per-route token telemetry; run A/B of cache on/off, batching profiles, and quantization candidate models; Redwood to provide recommended batching + cache config and an Optimize runbook.
AE notes: prioritize a short Dedicated sizing discussion mid-POC to prepare pricing options; include burst policy and preemption tolerances.
